where συνορθὸν ἀυταῖς [rising with the dawn] is in M, of which Wellauer corrected the first, Hermann the second. The sense is: the outcome will come with the light of the sun.
In the Florentine copy there is σύναρθρον ἀϋταῖς [joined with them], which Triclinius explained as συνηρμοσμένον βοαῖς καὶ θρήνοις [fitted to cries and laments].
For the future will come clear, rising with the dawn,
ὄρμενος [setting out] is an epic form of the aorist participle (Il. 11, 572), which the tragedians sometimes used for metrical reasons instead of ὀρόμενος [setting out]. See ὄρνυμαι [to set out].
From the land of Hellas, for those setting out together, sorrows befitting each house are fitting.
sister of clay, bordering thirsty dust.
to whom I came with harmless company.
The air is confounded with the sea.

About the assembly of the gods. As θεῶν πανάγυρις [the gathering of the gods] is said at v. 220. The scholiast: τὸ κοινὸν ἄθροισμα τῶν θεῶν, μεταφορικῶς. κυρίως γὰρ ἡ τῶν στρατιωτῶν ἄθροισις· τέλος γὰρ τὸ τάγμα. Ὅμηρος “ ἐλθεῖν ἐς φυλάκων ἱερὸν τέλος [the common gathering of the gods, metaphorically. For properly it is the gathering of soldiers; for a company is a division. Homer: to come to the sacred company of the guards]. The scholiast seems to interpret correctly, although this use of the word is unique. In vain Meinekius Philol. vol. 20 p. 56. ὦ Ζεῦ τέλειε [O Zeus the fulfiller], since Jupiter is invoked a little later at v. 255.
O assembly, do not betray the towers,
the common gathering of the gods, metaphorically. For properly it is the gathering of soldiers; for a company is a division. Homer: to come to the sacred company of the guards

Pollux 8, 156 συντελὴς ὁ σὺν ἄλλῳ λειτουργῶν, συντελῶν, συνεισφέρων, συνερανίζων [a contributor is one who performs public service with another, contributing, paying together, collecting together]. And Harpocration συντελεῖς: οἱ συνδαπανῶντες καὶ συνεισφέροντες [contributors: those who spend together and pay together].
which Triclinius explains as ή συντελέσασα καὶ συμπράξασα αὐτῷ [having accomplished and cooperated with him], i.e. joined with or obeying his command.
